title: Intacct Fundamentals at Greens
description: How Greens' ledger in Sage Intacct reaches you through Nexus Accounting: one ledger and two doors, entities, dimensions, journals and books, the reports and the drill-down, vendor and customer records, how Cubby money reaches the books, MRI, MRE and loans, AMA and the audit pages, the Dashboard and the close.
overview: One ledger, two doors: Intacct and Nexus Accounting
Dimensions: one account read by site, vendor or job
Vendor and customer records and change requests
How Cubby money reaches the books
MRI, MRE, loans and management fees
AMA, the reclass and the audit pages
The Dashboard, the close, reconciliations and the tools

lessons.checkpoint: Checkpoint: The Ledger and Its Reports

questions.q: Your report is missing a line you know was posted, and Sync did not bring it. What next?
questions.explanation: After Sync, a missing line is Accounting's question. Nothing is typed into Nexus, and switching the book or entity hides the problem rather than solving it.

questions.q: When a Nexus Accounting screen changes a loan's planning, it is changing a Nexus record beside the ledger, not the ledger.
questions.explanation: True. Loan planning, vendor papers and MRI or MRE expectations are Nexus's own records. The ledger itself is only changed in Intacct.

questions.q: You are limited to Temecula, entity 15001. Can you read lines coded 15001-1?
options: Yes, a parent brings its children
questions.explanation: 15001-1 is a sub-entity of 15001. Access to a parent includes its children, so the lines are yours to read.

questions.q: Your Spend by Vendor total for the year is far above your property's budget. What do you check first?
questions.explanation: A whole-company total compared to one property's budget always looks too big. Pick your entity first; the book does not change which properties are in it.

questions.q: Which journal carries vendor bills and their payments?
questions.explanation: Vendor bills and payments come through payables, APJ. Payroll carries wages; a statistical journal carries quantities, not dollars.

questions.q: A user-defined book's entries flow into the accrual statements.
questions.explanation: False. A user-defined book is accrual plus its own journals, and those entries stay in that book. They never leak into the accrual statements.

questions.q: On a screen outside Reports, a figure opens its lines in a side panel. How do you get the full grid?
questions.explanation: Open in Reports takes the lines to the full General Ledger grid. Memorize keeps a report view; Sync re-reads a table; Export makes a file.

questions.q: You need every transaction on one bank account for October. Where is that report?
questions.explanation: Bank Activity and Credit Card Activity sit under Reports > Banking & Credit Cards. Import Hub builds files for Intacct; it does not show the account's activity.

lessons.checkpoint: Checkpoint: Records, Cubby Money and the Close

questions.q: Who approves a change request on a vendor record?
options: The vendor, from an emailed link
Anyone at Viewer level on the grant
Cubby's billing team at the site
questions.explanation: A manager holding the Accounting grant, or someone at its Full level, decides it from Requests. Viewers can read but not decide, and vendors never approve their own record.

questions.q: Asset Management lists a pest vendor under the property's Records > Vendors. Is that the record Accounting pays?
options: No, Accounting pays the Intacct vendor
Yes, both lists are one record
Yes, once its COI is current
questions.explanation: The property's list is who services it, with contact and COI dates. The paying record is the Intacct vendor under Accounting > Records > Vendors.

questions.q: Where does a storage tenant's own ledger - charges, payments, balance - live?
questions.explanation: Tenants are billed and pay in Cubby. Intacct sees the money when it reaches the bank; only commercial lease tenants are Intacct customers.

questions.q: One bank deposit from the card processor can hold many tenants' payments from more than one day.
questions.explanation: True. Card and ACH payments are paid out in batches. Merchant Services Disbursements lists each batch and the payments inside it.

questions.q: Where is the actual on an MRI line taken from?
options: What posted to its income accounts
What the property manager types in each month
questions.explanation: MRI reads what posted to the line's income accounts for that customer. Only the expectation is kept in Nexus; nobody keys the actual.

questions.q: You want to see only the questions you asked on AMA. Which filter?
questions.explanation: Asked By Me shows your questions. Assigned To Me is for the accountant answering; Awaiting Bookkeeper is reclasses waiting for review.

questions.q: Nexus's Tools pages have a Post button the accounting team uses to post files to Intacct.
questions.explanation: False. Allocations and Import Hub prepare, preview and export files. The accounting team imports and posts them in Intacct.

questions.q: Which Dashboard pages need All Entities to open?
questions.explanation: Overview, Cash, Performance and Close all show the whole company added up, so all four need All Entities.

lessons.title: Words to Know
lessons.summary: The Intacct and Nexus Accounting words of this course, in the Academy glossary.

questions.q: A vendor payment is posted to the wrong property on your report. Where do you start the fix?
options: Edit the amount on the report in Nexus
Ask on the line through AMA
Re-key the payment on the Cash page
Change it on the vendor's Details tab
questions.explanation: Nexus never changes the ledger by typing. Ask on the line; the answer and the fix come back there. Editing a vendor's details files a request about the vendor, not the payment.

questions.q: A bill Accounting posted in Intacct an hour ago is not on your Income Statement. What do you do first?
options: Email the vendor for a copy of the bill
Type the bill into the report yourself
Assume it was never posted and wait a month
questions.explanation: Sync reads the report's table again from the ledger. If the line is still missing, ask Accounting. Nothing is ever typed into a report.

questions.q: A property manager with the Accounting grant and one entity can open the Dashboard's Overview page.
questions.explanation: False. Every Dashboard page shows the whole company added up, so it opens only for people with All Entities.

questions.q: A new manager should read only Murrieta's books. Where is that set?
options: The entity picker on each report
questions.explanation: Entity access is set under Tools > Access at the Full level. The entity picker only chooses among what she may already read.

questions.q: A coworker asks where Greens' books really live. What do you tell them?
questions.explanation: Intacct is the ledger and the source of truth. Nexus Accounting reads a copy; Cubby holds tenants' own ledgers.

questions.q: A line on Temecula's report carries code 15001-1, and the property is 15001. What is it?
questions.explanation: A suffix marks a sub-entity: part of the parent kept on its own books. A Construction job is tagged by Project-Job, not by an entity code.

questions.q: Your property report shows revenue three times what you expected. What do you check first?
questions.explanation: A report read for several entities, or all of them, adds them up. Check that only your property is picked.

questions.q: Running a report for a parent entity also brings in its sub-entities.
questions.explanation: True. A parent brings its children, and a person limited to the parent reads the children too.

questions.q: A property wants its covered rows kept on their own books as a sub-entity. How does that happen?
options: Add a row on Records > Entities
Accounting sets it up in Intacct
Type the new code on the next ticket
Create it from the entity picker
questions.explanation: Entities are made in Intacct by the accounting team. Records > Entities in Nexus is a reference list; it edits nothing.

questions.q: A Project-Job code appears on a canopy invoice line. What does it tell you?
options: Which property entity paid the bill
The Construction job the line belongs to
Which bank account it cleared from
Which person keyed it into Intacct
questions.explanation: Project-Job is the dimension that tags a Construction job's lines. The entity is a separate tag; a Project-Job is never an entity.

questions.q: The construction manager wants every cost on the canopy job, across all vendors. What is fastest?
options: A new GL account opened just for the job
Income Statement by Job, on its code
Spend by Vendor across every entity
A statement requested from each vendor
questions.explanation: Every line on the job carries its Project-Job code, so Income Statement by Job reads it in one step. A new account is never needed to slice by job.

questions.q: An invoice arrives with no ticket number and no property named. What is the risk?
options: It is paid twice by mistake
It may be coded to the wrong site
questions.explanation: The bookkeeper codes from what the site sent. With nothing to go on, the entity is a guess, and the cost can surprise another property's report.

questions.q: You want what one gate vendor was paid at your property this year. Which report?
questions.explanation: Spend by Vendor groups spending by vendor; pick your entity and the period. The vendor's Ledger Lines tab is the other way in.

questions.q: To read repairs by property, Intacct needs a separate repairs account for every property.
questions.explanation: False. Intacct keeps one repairs account and tags each line with its entity, so a filter reads it by property.

questions.q: A manager asks Accounting for a new 'Gate Repairs Murrieta' account. What is the better answer?
options: Open it and copy last year's lines
Filter the repairs account by entity
questions.explanation: Dimensions already tag every repairs line with its entity. A filter answers the question without changing the chart of accounts.

questions.q: Two October reports for one property disagree, and one was read on Cash. Why might they differ?
options: Cash leaves every vendor bill out of the month
Accrual counts rent when earned, Cash when paid
One report has a typing error
questions.explanation: October rent paid in early November is October on Accrual and November on Cash. Read both on the same book and they agree.

questions.q: A total on a report looks like it added hours to dollars. Which rule was broken?
options: Hours never add into money totals
questions.explanation: Hours are a statistical journal, and a statistical journal never adds into a money total. That is a question for Accounting.

questions.q: The Book picker's Accrual and Cash choice shows the two side by side as two columns.
questions.explanation: True. It is two reads of the same ledger, not a third book with entries of its own.

questions.q: You want only what posted through payroll last month. What do you use?
options: The Cash book on the Balance Sheet
The Budget page for the month
questions.explanation: The journal filter, or Records > Journals, shows what came through one journal. No account answers that question on its own.

questions.q: Unless you pick another, which book do Greens' statements use?
questions.explanation: Accrual is the default book and the one Greens reports on. Cash answers where money moved; a user-defined book has its own purpose.

questions.q: Repairs read $21,120 against a $14,000 budget. What is your first move?
options: Click the figure to open its lines
questions.explanation: Every posted figure opens its General Ledger lines, and each line opens its entry. The answer is usually two clicks away.

questions.q: You open a journal entry from a ledger line and need more room to read it. What do you click?
questions.explanation: Open Full spreads the side panel over the screen; Side Panel brings it back beside the list.

questions.q: You built a report in Report Builder and clicked Publish. Who can see it?
options: Only you, until you share it
questions.explanation: Publish finishes the report but keeps it yours. Share With Everyone is the step that shows it to others.

questions.q: A lender wants the same four statements for a property every quarter. What saves the most time?
questions.explanation: A Package keeps the set of memorized reports under one name; Build PDF reads each fresh and returns one PDF.

questions.q: On Budget vs. Actual, the budget figures open ledger lines when clicked.
questions.explanation: False. A budget is worked out, not posted, so it stays plain. The actual figures beside it drill down.

questions.q: You set up This Month vs. Last Month for your property and want it the same way next month. What do you click?
questions.explanation: Memorize keeps the view; a named period moves with the calendar. Publish belongs to Report Builder.

questions.q: You click the question mark at the end of a ledger line. What happens?
options: You ask My Accountant about it
questions.explanation: The question mark opens Ask My Accountant for that line. Nothing in Nexus deletes, edits or pushes a line from a report.

questions.q: You edit a vendor's address in Nexus. What happens in Intacct right away?
options: Nothing; a change request is filed
Intacct's record updates the same second
The vendor is marked inactive until checked
The vendor is emailed to confirm the change
questions.explanation: An edit files a change request with the fields that differ. Intacct changes only when Accounting keys the approved change.

questions.q: A vendor change reads Approved - Awaiting Intacct. What does that mean?
options: Approved, not yet keyed into Intacct
Declined; a new request is needed
Waiting for the vendor to sign
questions.explanation: It was approved and shows the new values, but checks still use Intacct's old ones until Accounting keys it in and it reads In Intacct.

questions.q: A roofer the ledger has never paid is booked for next week. What should happen first?
options: Accounting sets them up from their papers
Let them work now and sort out billing later
Pay the roofer on a card, then tell Accounting
Add them to the property's vendor list only
questions.explanation: A new vendor is set up in Intacct by Accounting. Send the license, insurance, workers comp and W-9 before the visit; no invoice is paid to a name the ledger lacks.

questions.q: Before a vendor's visit, where do you check that their insurance certificate is current?
questions.explanation: Compliance holds the insurance, workers comp and license dates and the W-9, with one state word such as Expiring Soon or Expired.

questions.q: A commercial lease tenant is set up as an Intacct customer.
questions.explanation: True. Most storage tenants live only in Cubby, but a commercial lease tenant is an Intacct customer, and MRI reads their rent from the ledger.

questions.q: A vendor record shows Changed In Intacct. What should you do before acting on it?
options: Approve the old request a second time
Delete the vendor and start over
Ignore it, because it clears by itself
questions.explanation: Intacct now holds a value different from what was approved. Look at the record before relying on either value.

questions.q: Cubby shows $18,240 in card payments this week, but the bank shows three deposits on different days. Why?
options: The bank holds deposits for a month
questions.explanation: The processor pays card and ACH money out in batches, so deposits do not line up one for one with payments or days.

questions.q: Which report ties each bank deposit to the card and ACH payments inside it?
questions.explanation: Merchant Services Disbursements, under Operations > Reports, lists each payout batch and the payments in it.

questions.q: A colleague asks which tenants are more than 90 days behind. Where do you look?
options: The Trial Balance for the property
questions.explanation: Tenant balances live in Cubby; Aged Receivables splits them into 30, 60, 90 and 120-day buckets. Most tenants are not Intacct customers.

questions.q: Import Hub's Bank Statement to Intacct posts the deposits straight into the ledger.
questions.explanation: False. It builds an Intacct import file. The accounting team imports and posts it in Intacct.

questions.q: The bank is $65 below Cubby's card total for the week. Where do you look first?
options: Budget vs. Actual for the month
questions.explanation: Receipts Summary counts failed and refunded payments, which explain a deposit lower than the day's takings.

questions.q: Fairfield's pest control line in MRE reads Missed for two months. What does it most likely mean?
options: The contract lapsed or billing stopped
The budget was set much too high
The entity was renamed in Intacct
questions.explanation: Missed means nothing posted when something should have. Call the vendor before it becomes a service gap or a surprise bill.

questions.q: A commercial tenant's lease ends and a new tenant moves in. What happens in MRI?
options: End the old line; add a new one
Delete the line and its history
questions.explanation: A lease is ended, never overwritten, so its history stands. The new tenant is a new line.

questions.q: An MRE line reads Over three months running. What should a manager suspect?
questions.explanation: Over means more posted than expected. A lapsed contract or a missed payment shows as Missed, not Over.

questions.q: A monthly mortgage payment belongs on Financing > Loans, not in MRE.
questions.explanation: True. Debt service is Loans, which reads its payments from the ledger. MRE is vendors paid on a schedule.

questions.q: A lender asks how a rate rise would hit a property's loan payment and DSCR. Where do you look?
questions.explanation: Stress Test, under Financing > Loans, shows what a higher rate does to each loan or across the portfolio.

questions.q: A property's Income Statement shows a management fee. What is it?
options: What the operator charges to run it
A late fee charged to tenants
A markup on vendor service calls
questions.explanation: A management fee is what the operating company charges a property entity for running it, set by the agreement on Management Fees.

questions.q: You sent a reclass with Pick GL. What does the line read until the bookkeeper acts?
questions.explanation: Send To Bookkeeper puts the line in Awaiting Bookkeeper. Pending Approval and Awaiting Intacct are vendor change request words.

questions.q: Who can push a reclass into Intacct?
questions.explanation: Anyone may ask and send a reclass; only a bookkeeper previews it and uses Approve & Push To Intacct.

questions.q: Preview Change shows the line's account before and after, and the amounts never change.
questions.explanation: True. Preview Change reads the original entry and shows exactly what moves: the line, its account and vendor or customer. Amounts stay as they are.

questions.q: Manual Journal Entries shows many entries for one month. What is the right reading?
options: Worth a question, not proof of error
Proof the month is full of errors
A fault in the bank feed rules
A sign that payroll ran twice
questions.explanation: The page lists hand-keyed and hand-changed entries so each can be seen. Most are right; a long list is a reason to ask.

questions.q: A manager wants wages per employee from Compensation. What does that page require?
options: Viewer level on any one entity
A manager role in any Nexus module
The PFS grant, held by owners
questions.explanation: Compensation and Payroll Summary open only at the Full level, and Compensation asks you to confirm it is you. Managers never see pay there.

questions.q: On AMA, which column tells you the bank or card the money came from?
questions.explanation: Other Side lists every account on the other side of the entry, so most questions are answered without a second click.

questions.q: You want to know whether the operating bank account is reconciled for October. Where do you look?
questions.explanation: Dashboard > Close lists every bank, card, mortgage, credit line and brokerage account with its reconciliation status.

questions.q: Who does the bank reconciliation itself?
questions.explanation: Accounting reconciles in Intacct. Nexus shows the status and opens each account's Bank Activity.

questions.q: Allocations posts the month's payroll split straight to Intacct.
questions.explanation: False. A kept run downloads as an Intacct CSV or Excel file; the accounting team posts it.

questions.q: On the fifth, Accounting asks about a $40,000 movement on your property. When should you answer?
questions.explanation: The close waits on variance answers. A same-day answer lets the line move to Answered and then Reviewed.

questions.q: You start next year's budget for one property. Which is a real starting point on the Budget page?
options: Copy From Cubby's Rent Roll Report
questions.explanation: The Budget page starts from Copy From Last Year's Actuals or Copy From Intacct Budget, then is edited in place.

questions.q: The Close page lists bank, credit card, mortgage, credit line and brokerage accounts with their reconciliation status.
questions.explanation: True. That is the Account Reconciliations card; click an account to open its activity already filtered.

questions.q: A number on a report surprises you. What is the first step the job aid gives?
options: Click it and read the lines
Rebuild it in a spreadsheet first
Ask the vendor for a copy
questions.explanation: Every posted figure clicks through to its lines and entries. Start there before asking anyone.
